analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (NemotronSuperVideoBindingTests.swift and NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift). No production code, key handling, attestation, coordinator protocol or cache code is modified in the supplied units, so no direct regression to the retained threat entries (A-001, TB-002, TB-007, T-041) is visible.

Security-relevant behavior the tests now pin, which the next pass should check against the unseen production changes:
(1) The video media charge is raised from 3,751,221,756 to 4,875,295,228 bytes (VideoBindingTests line 168). This implies a production change to Policy.videoMediaChargeBytes and the scoring or ingress accounting. The test still asserts video <= largest image charge and that ingress plus plan.totalBytes stays within the bound. The production budget and quote code is not supplied, so it cannot be verified that reservations still cover worst-case memory (a DoS and availability concern, T-010 and T-029 class).
(2) New test oversizeBodyIsMediaTooLarge (lines 233-242) expects Binding.Failure.bodyTooLarge to map to the mediaTooLarge code and invalidInput to map to invalidMedia. Status codes are asserted as 400, though the comment says 413 at the coordinator. Check the mapping is consistent with the coordinator contract and does not leak details.
(3) NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests line 241-245 now expects response_format json_object combined with tools to be accepted instead of refused. The output path withholds and validates JSON and tool calls (the existing testStructuredOutputIsWithheldValidatedAndNormalized and testToolPolicyViolationsFailClosed cover fail-closed validation), but the combined tools+JSON validation in production was not supplied. Confirm that it fails closed, so that unvalidated plaintext is never streamed and tool_choice enforcement is preserved.
(4) Making VideoOwner and videoOwner non-private is test visibility only. The test hook beforeFrameDecodeForTesting is a TaskLocal, and its production exposure should be confirmed to be non-reachable.

No finding is raised because only tests changed and the production sources are outside the supplied evidence.
